transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-21
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Ethan (Redwood SE); Dr. Maya, Omar, Jenna, Marcus (Pinehill)

Summary: Kickoff to onboard Pinehill Health onto Redwood for an initial 2-week pilot focused on clinical note summarization and QA. Discussed deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security/compliance certs, network requirements, pilot success metrics, and immediate next steps.

Topics: onboarding plan, connectivity, security (SOC2/KMS/RBAC), pilot benchmarks, rollouts, timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Samir from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We've got Lena our CSM and Ethan our solutions engineer with me. Hey team from Pinehill, could you do quick intros?
[00:10] Dr. Maya: Hi I’m Maya, head of clinical ops. We're excited to get Redwood in to help with note summarization and discharge workflows.
[00:15] Omar: Omar, CTO, I'm here to handle the network and infra questions.
[00:18] Jenna: Jenna, privacy officer, will be validating PHI handling and retention.
[00:21] Marcus: Marcus, IT lead, will work with Ethan on connectivity.
[00:25] Lena: Great — quick agenda, we want to align on pilots goals, security requirements, deployment mode, timeline, and owners.
[00:34] Ethan: I’ll also run through a high-level of the runtime and the staging steps so Marcus can see what to open in the firewall and what we need for KMS.
[00:40] Samir: Perfect. So goal for the pilot — two weeks of traffic on staging, run the summarization prompts, measure latency, correctness, and token-cost. Success metric from you Maya?
[00:49] Dr. Maya: Ideally summary accuracy above 90% on our sanity set and average latency under 600ms for a single patient note, but we're flexible if you recommend stricter.
[00:58] Ethan: Quick note — hosted mode can get you up fast, typically lower ops overhead, but if PHI retention or KMS integration is required, Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) is usually the path customers take. There's also Dedicated reserved capacity if you want predictable throughput.
[01:12] Jenna: PHI is a hard requirement — we need KMS that integrates with our HSM and detailed audit logs. SOC 2 is table stakes. Does Redwood have those?
[01:20] Lena: Yes — we are SOC 2 Type II certified, and we have KMS integrations with customer-managed keys and audit logs. I'll attach the SOC2 report and the security pack after this call.
[01:28] Jenna: Great. Also retention policies; we can't keep raw PHI in any logs beyond 30 days, and we need exportability for audits.
[01:35] Samir: Understood — we can set token-level retention, and we support configurable retention and export. I'll have Lena include the specifics.
[01:42] Marcus: From a network perspective, what's required? Do we need VPN? IP allowlists?
[01:46] Ethan: We support several patterns: VPC peering, private link, and simple IP allowlists for hosted. For Private/private control plane deployments you can run within your VPC and use KMS. For the pilot, if you want low friction, we often do IP allowlist + restricted staging workspace; for production you can move to VPC peering.
[02:02] Marcus: Ok, I'll pull firewall team and share our egress ranges and peering contact.
[02:07] Omar: How about throughput — we expect bursts during end-of-day processing. Do you autoscale?
[02:12] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Dedicated provides reserved capacity with autoscaling policies. For pilot we can simulate your burst profile to size the Dedicated pool if you go that route. For hosted, there can be variability but we can set concurrency limits.
[02:26] Dr. Maya: Pricing — do you have an estimate for cost during pilot vs production?
[02:30] Samir: I'll send a tailored pricing summary. Pilot cost is usually minimal; production will depend on throughput and model choice. We'll include token estimates in the doc.
[02:38] Jenna: Also need to know where data is stored — region/residency?
[02:41] Lena: We can pin region for data residency. For your account we can use US-East region and avoid cross-region replication unless requested.
[02:49] Marcus: Marcus -> also KMS — who do we talk to on your side for integrating our key management?
[02:54] Ethan: That's usually me and our infra partner. I'll add a short integration checklist in the benchmark plan.
[03:00] Samir: Ok quick walkthrough of pilot timeline: Week 0 (this week) — sign off on security docs, provide connectivity details, we provision staging keys; Week 1 — run sample load and tune prompts/latency; Week 2 — run comparative QA, capture metrics, decision point for Dedicated or Private.
[03:18] Dr. Maya: That sounds good. Who's owner for the pilot execution?
[03:21] Lena: We'll be the primary CSM — I (Lena) will coordinate, Samir will handle commercial items, Ethan will run the benchmarks with Marcus.
[03:29] Omar: Are there known model recommendations for clinical summarization? Any regulated model list?
[03:34] Ethan: We have a model catalog; for clinical tasks we recommend closers models with instruction tuning and medically-aligned evals — we can propose three candidate models and quantization profiles to balance cost and latency. There may be some mis-says in the catalog but we’ll validate.
[03:48] Dr. Maya: Important: outputs must be explainable; we need minimal hallucination. Do you support soft prompts or controlled generation?
[03:55] Ethan: Yes, you can use system prompts, controlled decoding and structured output (JSON schema) to reduce hallucinations. We also support evaluations and regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[04:06] Marcus: On the technical side, what's the inference latency expectation for a note of 1-2k tokens?
[04:11] Ethan: On GPU-backed Dedicated we often see 200-400ms for shorter context; for larger contexts 600-800ms depending on model and batch settings. We'll benchmark with your actual note sizes.
[04:23] Dr. Maya: Ok — we prefer latency under 600ms as a target for now.
[04:27] Samir: Noted. Any blockers on your side?
[04:29] Omar: Need to confirm legal on data processing agreement, and get network windows for peering work. Jenna will confirm PHI specifics.
[04:36] Jenna: Also, encryption at rest and in transit details; please include cipher suites and key rotation cadence in the security pack.
[04:42] Lena: We'll include that. We'll also share a runbook for incident handling and SLOs.
[04:48] Samir: Quick demo note — Ethan, can you show the simplest flow to ingest a batch of notes and call the summarization endpoint?
[04:53] Ethan: Sure, high level — we have a small agent and an ingestion pipeline; you can hit the Redwood API with a request that includes model, system prompt, and your content. For staged pilot we'll share sample curl and Python snippets; if you want streaming or function calling we can demo that too.
[05:09] Dr. Maya: Is there an SDK in Java and Python? Our stack is mostly Python.
[05:12] Samir: Yes Python SDK and REST are supported; we also have examples for Node.
[05:17] Marcus: For staging keys — how long are keys valid? Can we rotate automatically?
[05:21] Lena: Keys can be rotated; for customer-managed KMS you control rotation. For hosted keys we have rotation policies.
[05:26] Omar: Any limitations around on-prem models? Could we host the model in our datacenter?
[05:29] Ethan: We do offer an on-prem package for air-gapped or regulated workloads but that is a separate enterprise engagement. For the pilot, we usually do private VPC or hosted with strict retention.
[05:39] Dr. Maya: Great. On pilot success we'll want to expand to discharge automation in Q4. Is that realistic?
[05:44] Samir: Yes — if pilot metrics look good we can scope production rollout and a phased integration with EHR.
[05:50] Marcus: Scheduling — when can we get the SOC2 doc and the network checklist?
[05:53] Lena: I'll send those by end of day tomorrow.
[05:56] Samir: And I'll send the pricing summary and the onboarding guide. Ethan, you'll own the benchmark plan?
[06:01] Ethan: Yes, I’ll share by next Monday.
[06:04] Dr. Maya: Sounds good. Any final Qs?
[06:08] Jenna: One more — audit logs format, are they exportable to our SIEM?
[06:12] Ethan: Yes, logs can be exported to S3 or pushed via forwarders to your SIEM; we'll include the schema in the security pack.
[06:19] Samir: Amazing — quick recap of next steps: Samir sends pricing and onboarding guide; Lena sends SOC2 and security pack; Ethan shares benchmark plan and sample prompt sets; Marcus and Omar supply network/KMS details; Jenna confirms retention policy. We'll meet again in 1 week for a quick sync and then kick off the pilot the week after.
[06:36] Dr. Maya: Thanks everyone. Excited to get started.
[06:40] Samir: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

Notes on transcription: occasional misrecognitions of product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" transcribed as "Red wood dedicated"), filler words, and brief crosstalk.

Referenced artifacts/links:
- Onboarding guide (will be sent)
- SOC2 & security pack (Lena to attach)
- Sample prompts and benchmark spreadsheet (Ethan)

End of call.
